bottlenecks_identified: The bottleneck this turn is in the retro-generation pipeline, not the experiment layer: a git-log check performed this turn (outside the authoritative TIMING DATA block, so it did not touch any locked field) shows dozens of real commits landed after this milestone's activation commit, spanning several distinct PHASE-lettered experiment tasks -- yet the TIMING DATA source supplied to this retro still reads zero.

The gap has not been escalated into ops/known-issues.md's MANDATORY-NEXT-MILESTONE PRIORITIES list -- a search this turn for the fix module's name and for the general 'false-zero timing' phrasing in that file returns no hits -- so the project's own mechanical Overdue-Priority Forcing Function (which forces planner pickup once an entry has been pending 3+ milestones) has nothing to act on, even though this same empty-window symptom has now produced three consecutive retro passes for this one milestone.

This retro-generation task's own instructions explicitly forbid editing scripts/research_conductor.py, so even though the fix appears to be a small, already-documented change, it structurally cannot be applied from within a retro turn -- nothing currently routes the wiring work to a task type that is both allowed to touch that file and aware the gap needs closing.
